system_implications: The MBR defines a pre-filtration bioburden sampling point (for example, at the end of the bulk hold, immediately before sterilising filtration) together with its limit and method. The eBMR generates the sampling task, captures sample ID and time, and links the LIMS result. A result above the limit triggers a deviation. Release requires the result. Results are trended per product.
verification_test: Execute a batch without taking the pre-filtration bioburden sample: filtration start must be blocked. Post a result above the limit: a deviation must be created and linked, and release blocked pending assessment.

requirement: Other microbiological methods, such as rapid methods, can be used for EM, in-process testing and release testing once they have been shown to be equivalent to or better than traditional (for example USP) methods.
system_implications: Result records carry a method ID with its validation or equivalence reference. The release rules accept a result only when its method is approved for that test type and product, so rapid methods can be used without special handling while unvalidated methods are refused.
verification_test: Link a rapid-method bioburden result whose method has no approved equivalence record: the release check must refuse it. Approve the method: the same check must accept it.

requirement: Routine particle monitoring quickly detects departures from qualified air cleanliness. Any result above the classification level at a location should be investigated for cause. The depth of the investigation should match how severe the excursion was and include a review of trend data, with corrective action taken as needed to stop it happening again.
system_implications: Particle excursions during the batch window are imported as events linked to the batch, recording location, magnitude, duration and severity category. Each must have an investigation or assessment record, sized to its severity, that includes a trend look-up. Unassessed particle excursions block the batch review.
verification_test: Inject a 3-minute excursion to 10,000 particles per m3 at the needle location during filling. It must appear on the batch timeline linked to concurrent interventions, and review sign-off must be blocked until it has been assessed.

requirement: Sterility test methods are required to be accurate and reproducible, with validation and documentation per 211.165 and 211.194. USP <71> is the main reference. Method validation should show that representative organisms are reliably recovered in the presence of the product, and the method should be modified (dilution, extra rinses, neutralisers) if growth is inhibited, so there is no opportunity for false negatives.
system_implications: The release gate accepts a sterility result only if the linked test record references a method-suitability (bacteriostasis/fungistasis) validation that is approved for this product and formulation, and whose version is current at the test date. A change to the product formulation invalidates that link until re-verified.
verification_test: Change the product's formulation version, then link a sterility result whose method suitability was done on the old formulation: the release check must flag it and refuse to release.

requirement: The sterility testing environment should have facilities and controls comparable to aseptic filling; isolators reduce false positives. If the lab is weaker than production, a real product failure risks being blamed on the lab. Test media should be sterile and proven to support growth. Analysts should be qualified and trained, with a written program that keeps training current and confirms good test practice.
system_implications: A sterility result linked to the batch must carry the test environment (isolator or cleanroom ID and its status), media lots with sterility and growth-promotion status, analyst ID with qualification valid on the test date, and the incubation start and end dates. The release check flags any missing or non-compliant element for QA review.
verification_test: Link a sterility result where the analyst's sterility-testing qualification expired before the test date: release review must flag it and need QA justification or retest per procedure.

requirement: Because the sterility test samples so few units, it has limited power. For example, a lot with 0.1% contaminated units tested with 20 units passes about 98% of the time. Samples should therefore represent the whole batch and its processing conditions. They should be taken at the start, middle and end of the aseptic operation, and also in connection with interventions or excursions. Any positive is a serious CGMP issue that needs thorough investigation.
system_implications: The eBMR generates sterility sample-pull tasks at defined fill-progress points (beginning, middle, end, based on unit count or elapsed time). It also generates extra sample-pull tasks automatically after a defined intervention or an environmental excursion. For each pull it records unit, tray position and time. The release check confirms all required pull points were sampled and tested. For lyophilised product, sample-to-lyo-load mapping is kept where multiple loads exist.
verification_test: Log a major intervention at 40% fill: an extra sterility sample task must be generated for the units filled right after it. Close the fill with the 'middle' sample missing: the system must flag incomplete sampling and block release.

requirement: If growth appears in a sterility test, the lot should be treated as non-sterile and investigated. A first positive can be invalidated only when the growth is unequivocally shown to come from laboratory error, and a retest is justified only by conclusive, documented evidence that contamination happened during testing. If the evidence is inconclusive, the batch should be rejected as failing sterility. Any testing deviation should be documented, investigated and fixed, and a test whose integrity was compromised should be invalidated immediately, before incubation.
system_implications: A positive sterility result automatically sets the batch to 'sterility failure: presumed non-sterile' and blocks release. A retest can only be linked after QA approves an invalidation record that has attached evidence of laboratory cause. If QA signs 'inconclusive', the only disposition allowed is rejection. Original results are kept and never replaced by retests. Lab-invalidated tests, meaning those stopped before incubation, are visible in the batch record together with their deviation reference.
verification_test: Post a positive result, then try to link a passing retest without an approved invalidation: this must be refused. Record the investigation outcome as 'inconclusive': the release option must be disabled and only 'reject' offered.

requirement: A sterility-positive investigation should end in written specific conclusions and corrective actions, supported by evidence. That evidence should include: species ID of the isolate, compared with EM, personnel and bioburden isolates using the same ID method; the lab's deviation and test records and lab EM trends; short- and long-term production EM trends, not only the lot's own day or shift; personnel monitoring trends and practices; pre-sterilisation bioburden trends; a full review of batch and production records for events affecting the critical zone, utility or support-system problems (for example air imbalance or high particles), and construction or maintenance; and the manufacturing history of the product and similar products, meaning past deviations and changes. Because the cause may extend beyond one batch, the whole process should be investigated. Under 211.192 the investigation must extend to other associated batches.
system_implications: The sterility-failure investigation template is pre-filled from the eBMR data model with: the batch's interventions, alarms, dP and particle excursions, and utility events; EM results for the batch window plus a configurable look-back and look-forward trend; personnel monitoring for the batch roster; bioburden trend; filter integrity and sterilisation records; maintenance and construction work orders for the rooms; and prior deviations and changes. It also proposes the associated batches: those sharing the same line, filling window, sterilisation loads, bulk, component lots or personnel.
verification_test: Trigger a sterility positive and check the investigation opens with all evidence sections pre-filled. Check that the associated-batch list includes batches that shared the same autoclave load of filling parts.

requirement: Keep separate sterility-failure trends by product, container type, filling line, and sampling and testing personnel. Where sample handling in the lab is similar, a higher initial failure rate for aseptically filled product than for terminally sterilised product suggests problems in aseptic production. Upward trends in the lab's aseptic-area counts should be investigated promptly and fixed. A lab's poor track record must not be used to automatically blame the lab and miss a real production problem.
system_implications: Each sterility test record carries these attributes: product, container type, filling line, sterilisation mode (aseptic, terminal), sampler, analyst and test environment. This supports the required trend views, including initial-positive rate for aseptic versus terminal sterilisation. The investigation form does not allow 'lab error' as a conclusion without specific evidence, whatever the lab's history.
verification_test: Produce the initial-positive trend by line and by sterilisation mode from test data and check it against a manual count. Try to close an investigation citing 'lab error' with no evidence attachment: this must be refused.

requirement: Before a batch is released or distributed, the quality unit must review and approve all production and control records, including packaging and labelling, to confirm the approved procedures were followed. Any unexplained discrepancy, including yield outside the MPCR limits, and any failure of the batch or a component to meet specifications must be thoroughly investigated, even if the batch has already shipped. The investigation must extend to other batches and products that may be affected, and must be written up with conclusions and follow-up.
system_implications: Release is a QA e-signature that is only available once every section of the batch record is complete. That includes all review-by-exception items being dispositioned, every deviation and investigation closed or formally assessed as not affecting this batch, and yield and reconciliation (liquid bulk, fill count, inspection, labelling) within MPCR limits or explained. Investigations must record which other batches or products they checked, and the conclusions and follow-up.
verification_test: Leave one deviation open and one yield outside limits, then attempt release: it must be refused, listing both items. Close the investigation without filling the 'other batches assessed' field: closure must be refused.

requirement: For an aseptically processed product, every IPC and lab control result has to form part of the documentation for the batch record.
system_implications: The MBR declares a required-results list: bioburden, filter integrity tests, fill weights and volumes, IPC functional tests, EM and personnel monitoring, sterility, endotoxin, release assays and so on. The eBMR links each one as an immutable reference to the source record (LIMS or EMS) with its value, limit and status, and prints or renders it in the executed batch record. The release check confirms every required result is present, approved and in the batch record, not just in the LIMS.
verification_test: Remove the link to the post-use filter integrity result: the completeness check must fail. Change a LIMS result after it was linked: the eBMR must show the revision history and require re-review.

requirement: Process and environmental controls should be built into daily aseptic operations and strictly maintained. Before the release decision, the batch records and data are reviewed against procedures, operating parameters and specifications, which amounts to a holistic assessment of how the process and its supporting systems performed during that production run. The guidance treats these as essential elements of the release decision: review of EM and personnel monitoring data; data showing support systems gave acceptable output (HEPA/HVAC, WFI, steam generator); and evidence that equipment worked properly (for example the batch alarm report and integrity of the various filters).
system_implications: The eBMR assembles a sterile batch review dossier with signed-off sections. These cover EM (viable and non-viable) for every room and zone in the batch window, personnel monitoring for the roster, HVAC/HEPA status and dP, WFI and clean-steam results for the period, the equipment and EMS alarm report, all filter integrity results (product, vent and gas), sterilisation and depyrogenation cycles, interventions and stoppages, time-limit compliance, and media-fill and qualification status. Each section needs reviewer sign-off, and QA release is blocked until every section is signed.
verification_test: Leave the WFI section unsigned and try to release: this must be refused. Inject a WFI TOC or conductivity OOS during the batch window: it must appear in the dossier needing assessment.

requirement: Interventions and stoppages are normally recorded in the batch record, but in inconsistent ways. Line stoppages and any unplanned interventions should be documented well enough, with the time and duration of each event. Extensive interventions both lengthen the time sterile items spend in the critical zone and add contamination risk, and sterility failures have often been traced to atypical or extensive interventions made in response to problems during filling. Major interventions such as machine adjustments or repairs should be documented in more detail than minor events.
system_implications: The intervention/stoppage log captures start and end time (with duration calculated), catalogue type, whether it was inherent or corrective, location on the line, people involved (checked against their media-fill qualification), units removed, and whether line clearance was performed. For corrective or major interventions it also requires what failed, what was adjusted or replaced, the tools and parts used with their sterilisation records, and immediate EM or personnel sampling where configured. Machine-stop events from the line PLC or SCADA are reconciled against the log, and unexplained stops are flagged for review.
verification_test: Replay a PLC stop of 7 minutes with no matching intervention entry: the review must flag an unexplained stoppage. Log a corrective intervention without the 'parts replaced' field: saving must be refused.

requirement: Written procedures should say when interventions such as machine adjustments or repairs require line clearance. An intervention that involves substantial activity near exposed product or container-closures, or that goes beyond a reasonable exposure time, should lead to a local or full line clearance where appropriate.
system_implications: Each catalogue entry defines the required clearance (none, local or full) and the maximum duration or exposure before clearance becomes mandatory. When an intervention needs clearance, or runs over its maximum, the eBMR will not allow line restart until a clearance record is complete. That record states the scope, the units and positions removed, and the reconciliation of removed units. Removed units are excluded from good output and accounted for in yield.
verification_test: Log a filling-needle realignment (catalogue: local clearance) and try to restart without a clearance record: this must be blocked. Log a routine weight check exceeding its 3-minute maximum: clearance must be forced.

requirement: Any interruption of the power supply that could affect product quality, however brief, is a manufacturing deviation and must be recorded in the batch record.
system_implications: Power events for the batch's rooms, line equipment, HVAC, EMS and sterilisers (from UPS, BMS or equipment logs, with manual entry as a fallback) are imported for the batch window. Each event automatically creates a deviation linked to the batch, even if brief, containing the equipment affected, duration and recovery actions. Release is blocked until the deviation is assessed.
verification_test: Inject a 2-second power dip on the filling machine feed during filling: a deviation must be auto-created, linked, and shown in the batch record. Release must be refused until the deviation is closed.

requirement: Written production and process control procedures, approved by the quality unit, must be followed and documented at the time each activity is performed. Any departure from them must be recorded and justified. Master records and batch records must meet 211.186 and 211.188.
system_implications: All aseptic steps are recorded as they happen, with server-synchronised timestamps and attributed e-signatures. Late or back-dated entries are flagged and need a reason. A deviation record with justification is required whenever execution departs from the MBR, such as a skipped or out-of-order step, a parameter outside its range, or a substitute piece of equipment. The MBR, including all Injectables-specific rules, is version-controlled and QA-approved.
verification_test: Enter a step completion 3 hours after the recorded activity: the entry must be flagged 'late' with a reason required. Try to execute a step out of sequence: a deviation must be required. Check that the MBR cannot be used until QA has approved it.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.67(a), 211.113(b) (inferred)
requirement: A leak in an isolator's gloves, sleeves, half-suits or seams is a serious integrity breach. These parts need daily attention and a preventive-maintenance program, with written replacement frequencies that ensure parts are changed before they degrade. Transfer systems, gaskets and seals should be covered too. Gloves should be visually checked for obvious defects every time they are used, and physically integrity-tested routinely. Any glove lacking integrity should be removed from service. Because microscopic holes may go undetected, attention to the inner-glove surface and wearing a thin second pair of gloves are recommended.
system_implications: A glove/sleeve/half-suit register per isolator port holds the item ID, installation date, replacement due date, and the last physical integrity test and result. Before each batch, the eBMR requires a signed visual inspection for every port that will be used, and checks that each port's integrity test and replacement dates are current. A port that fails or is overdue cannot be used. If a glove fails a test after use, the system links the failure to every batch processed since that glove last passed, for impact assessment.
verification_test: Set glove port 3 as overdue for replacement: the pre-use check must block the batch or require a deviation. Record a post-campaign leak-test failure on port 2: the impacted-batch list must be generated and holds applied.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.42(c)(10)(iii)-(iv) (inferred)
requirement: Isolators should keep a qualified positive pressure against the room (typically about 17.5-50 Pa, depending on design and exit port). Air balance with directly connected equipment such as a depyrogenation tunnel should also be qualified. Openings should be designed so room air cannot be drawn in, for example with local ISO 5 protection. The interior should be ISO 5. The background room is set by interface design and transfer frequency (commonly ISO 8) and should never be unclassified. Rapid transfer ports work well, but weaker ports need local HEPA unidirectional cover. Overpressure at the product exit (mousehole) should be supplied and monitored continuously.
system_implications: The eBMR links continuous isolator internal pressure and exit-port overpressure data for the batch window and compares it with each isolator's qualified limits. Excursions become integrity-breach events (see ASEP-97). Every material transfer into or out of the isolator is logged: port type, transfer ID, item, and how it was sterilised or decontaminated. The background room's class and status are checked at batch start.
verification_test: Replay exit-port overpressure dropping to 0 Pa for 20 s during filling: an integrity-breach event must be created and linked to the batch. Record a transfer through a UV pass-box without the required local HEPA cover status: it must be flagged.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.113(b) (inferred)
requirement: Decontamination should reach every isolator surface: gloves fully extended with fingers apart, and the interior cleaned first. The cycle should leave inner surfaces free of viable organisms. It should be validated with quantified biological indicators on a range of materials and in many locations, including hard-to-reach spots, with a margin of extra kill (usually a 4-6 log reduction, and 4 log can be enough for low-bioburden wrapped items brought into a transfer isolator). Validation should also show uniform distribution of the agent, and chemical indicators can confirm the agent reached a location.
system_implications: The eBMR decontamination step records confirmation of pre-cleaning and of glove extension, the validated cycle recipe ID, key cycle parameters (for example agent amount or concentration, phase durations, and end-of-aeration residual below its limit), any chemical indicator results, and pass or fail. The isolator is not released for aseptic work until a passing cycle is recorded, and the cycle ID is linked to the batch.
verification_test: Record a cycle where the aeration residual reading is above its limit: the isolator must stay in 'not released' status and filling must be blocked. Skip the glove-extension confirmation: the cycle record must not be completable.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.192 (inferred)
requirement: Isolators should be decontaminated often. If one is used for several days between cycles, the interval should be justified by validation and shortened if data show the isolator's microbial quality getting worse. A loss of integrity, from causes such as power or valve failure, insufficient overpressure, glove or seam holes or other leaks, should normally trigger decontamination and an investigation. If the environment may have been compromised, any product that could be affected should be rejected.
system_implications: Isolator status holds 'decontaminated, valid until', calculated from the validated interval, and the eBMR blocks aseptic steps after that time. Integrity-breach events (from dP data, glove tests, power or valve alarms) set the isolator to 'decontamination required' and create a deviation linked to the batch. The deviation has a unit-impact field: units filled during the suspect window default to rejection unless QA records a documented justification that the environment was not compromised. Deteriorating EM trends raise a prompt to review the interval.
verification_test: Let the validated 7-day interval run out mid-campaign: the next fill step must be blocked. Record a glove hole found at 14:00 with last pass at 08:00: units filled 08:00-14:00 must default to rejection pending QA decision.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.113(b); 211.67 (inferred)
requirement: The whole sterile processing stream should be sterilised so product-contact surfaces are sterile from the start of every operation. Equipment and supplies for use inside the isolator should be chosen so they can be steam-sterilised or equivalent, and materials that tolerate heat (for example by SIP) are expected to be heat-sterilised. Where surface decontamination is used to make a product-contact surface free of viable organisms, it should show at least a 6-log reduction with a suitable BI.
system_implications: In the MBR, every product-contact item has a declared method: SIP, autoclave, or decontamination. For 'decontamination' the MBR cannot be approved without a validation reference proving a 6-log reduction or more, while heat-tolerant parts cannot be assigned decontamination. At execution, the eBMR requires the matching sterilisation or SIP record for each item.
verification_test: Assign VHP decontamination to a stainless filling needle (heat-tolerant): MBR approval must be refused. Assign it to a heat-labile sensor with a 6-log validation reference: approval must be allowed.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.42(c)(10)(iv) (inferred)
requirement: Isolator EM should routinely cover air, surfaces, gloves or half-suits, and particles inside the isolator. Medium left on surfaces after contact plating should be wiped off. Air quality should be checked periodically in every shift, with particle monitoring at the exit port recommended. EM media should never be exposed to decontamination residues, which would suppress recovery.
system_implications: The isolator EM plan generates glove-fingertip samples for each glove port used in the batch, as well as air, surface and exit-port particle tasks per shift. After contact plating, a confirmation that the surface was wiped is required. The eBMR enforces sequencing: EM media cannot be introduced or exposed until the decontamination aeration phase is recorded as complete.
verification_test: Try to log settle-plate exposure start before the decontamination aeration end time: this must be blocked. Record a contact plate without the wipe-down confirmation: the task must stay incomplete.

requirement: Even though gowning demands are lower with isolators, manual work through gloves and half-suits still carries risk: those are hard to decontaminate and glove defects may go unnoticed. Contaminated isolator gloves can make product non-sterile, so rigorous aseptic technique must be observed, including using sterile tools for manipulations.
system_implications: Glove-port manipulations in isolators are logged in the intervention log like cleanroom interventions: type, port, duration and operator, with the operator's media-fill and qualification checked. Each tool used is linked to its sterilisation record. Personnel monitoring for isolator operators includes the glove-port gloves they used.
verification_test: Log an isolator intervention using a tool with no sterilisation record: the entry must be refused. Check that isolator interventions appear in the same review section as cleanroom interventions.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.113(b); 211.42(c)(10) (inferred)
requirement: The guidance's aseptic standards apply to blow-fill-seal (BFS) unless stated otherwise. The steps most exposed to contamination are cutting the parison, moving it under the fill mandrel, and withdrawing the mandrel before sealing. The product path should be sterilised by a validated SIP or equivalent, and any other surface that could contaminate product should also be sterile. The room around the machine should generally be ISO 8 or better. HEPA-filtered or sterile membrane-filtered air should be used whenever product or materials are exposed (parison forming, moulding, filling). The critical zone should meet ISO 5 microbial limits during operation and normally ISO 5 particle levels. Only qualified, gowned staff should enter the surrounding classified room.
system_implications: The BFS line template requires: the product-path SIP cycle record, checked against its validated recipe; filter IDs and integrity status for the sterile process-air filters; confirmation that the background room is ISO 8 or better; critical-zone viable and particle monitoring against ISO 5 limits across the run; and the personnel qualification gates from Section V.
verification_test: Start a BFS run whose SIP record is outside its validated temperature range: this must be blocked. Record a parison-support air filter with an expired integrity test: the step must be blocked.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.67(a) (inferred)
requirement: Particles from extrusion, cutting and sealing should be controlled through airflow design, separation of the filling zone, and similar measures, with smoke studies and particle data from multiple locations used in qualification. A sound preventive-maintenance program is needed. The cooling, heating and other utility systems attached to the BFS machine can contaminate product, so their integrity should be maintained and routinely monitored.
system_implications: At batch start the eBMR checks that BFS machine preventive maintenance and the machine-utility integrity checks (for example mould-cooling circuit leak checks) are current. It imports machine utility alarms for the batch window into the batch alarm report, and blocks or deviation-gates a batch on a machine with overdue preventive maintenance or an open utility-integrity failure.
verification_test: Mark the mould-cooling integrity check as overdue: the batch start must be blocked or deviation-gated. Inject a chiller alarm during the run: it must appear in the batch alarm report needing assessment.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.113(b); 211.84 (inferred)
requirement: BFS set-up, equipment troubleshooting and the associated aseptic procedures deserve special attention. Validation should cover equipment sterilisation, media fills, polymer extrusion and its sterilising effect, compatibility between product and plastic, integrity of forming and sealing, and variation in unit weight. The extrusion time and temperature should be shown to deal with endotoxin or spore challenges, so containers are sterile and, for parenterals, non-pyrogenic. The polymer should be pharmaceutical grade and pass the relevant plastics criteria, and polymer suppliers should be qualified and monitored.
system_implications: The eBMR records the extrusion parameters (for example melt temperature and residence time) against the validated range for the run. It records the polymer lot and checks that the lot is released and the supplier is qualified. It logs set-up and troubleshooting activities as interventions, with media-fill coverage checked.
verification_test: Import an extrusion melt temperature below the validated minimum for 15 minutes: the affected units must be flagged and a deviation required. Issue a resin lot from a supplier whose qualification has lapsed: this must be blocked.

requirement: In-process parameters such as container weight variation, fill weight, leakers and air pressure support ongoing process control. Microbial air monitoring is essential and should follow a comprehensive plan that represents the whole fill, and continuous particle monitoring is valuable. The line should be set up to make integral units consistently, and every unit should get a reliable, sensitive final examination able to catch defects such as leakers. Significant defects from heat or mechanical causes (wall thickness, container or closure interface problems, badly formed closures) should be investigated in line with 211.100 and 211.192.
system_implications: The BFS MBR defines the IPC schedule (container weight, fill weight, leak checks, process air pressure) and an EM plan that spreads samples across the whole run. Results are captured against limits. A 100% leak-detection or inspection step records method, equipment, challenge or verification result, and reject counts by defect type. Any significant forming or sealing defect automatically creates a deviation with a 211.192 investigation.
verification_test: Enter a wall-thickness defect cluster: a deviation must be auto-created. Try to complete the batch with the leak-detection verification check (known-defect challenge) missing: completion must be blocked.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.113(b); 21 CFR 610.12 for biologics (footnote)
requirement: Some products must be handled aseptically from early steps onwards: after a point beyond which they cannot be filtered, or when the final product cannot be sterile-filtered, so each component is sterilised and mixed aseptically (for example aluminium-adjuvanted vaccines). Every transfer, transport and storage stage then needs tight control, and bulk may in some cases need sterility testing. Steps that expose product or contact surfaces, such as aseptic connections, should happen under ISO 5 unidirectional air with an ISO 7 or better background. Microbial and particle monitoring should run during operations, surface sampling should be done at the end but before cleaning, and personnel monitoring should accompany the operations.
system_implications: Bulk and formulation-stage MBRs support aseptic connection steps with ISO 5 and background class checks, EM and personnel-monitoring task generation, and sequencing so the end-of-operation surface EM comes before the cleaning step. They also cover sterile bulk transfer and transport logs (vessel ID, integrity or pressure status, route, times) and a bulk sterility sample linked to its result where the MBR requires it.
verification_test: Try to sign the post-formulation cleaning step before the surface EM samples are recorded: this must be blocked. Try to use bulk that needs a sterility test and has no result: the downstream step must be blocked.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.113(b); 211.111 (inferred)
requirement: Process simulations of the steps before filling should include every manipulation, addition and exposure of contact surfaces that could affect sterility, under worst-case conditions such as the longest open operations and the most operators. They need not match total manufacturing time if the manipulations are fully represented. They should also cover storage and transport of sterile bulk, with assurance that bulk vessels stay intact for the specified hold times. The formulation-stage simulation should be performed at least twice a year.
system_implications: The formulation or bulk stage has its own process-simulation status: six-monthly, with an envelope for maximum open-operation time, maximum operators, and maximum sterile-bulk hold and transport time. The eBMR checks this status before aseptic formulation. It enforces sterile-bulk hold time as no longer than the validated vessel-integrity hold, and flags any execution outside the envelope as a deviation.
verification_test: Let the formulation-stage simulation become 7 months old: aseptic compounding must be blocked. Hold sterile bulk 10 days against an 8-day validated vessel-integrity hold: a deviation must be required.

binding_basis: none named in appendix; related 21 CFR 211.167(a); 211.165(a) (inferred)
requirement: Cell therapy and some cell-derived products cannot be filter-sterilised and are handled aseptically throughout, ideally in closed systems. They are often given to patients before final sterility results are available. In that case additional controls should be considered, such as sterility tests at intermediate stages (for example after the last manipulation before harvest). Rapid indicators such as microscopy, Gram or other stains, and endotoxin should pass before release.
system_implications: This is an optional module, outside the core Injectables scope. It provides a conditional-release workflow where release before the final sterility result requires passing intermediate sterility, stain and endotoxin results. The final sterility result is tracked afterwards, and a positive result triggers an escalation and notification path.
verification_test: With the module enabled, try to release with the Gram stain result missing: this must be refused. Post a late positive final sterility result on a released lot: the escalation workflow must be triggered.

requirement: The guidance does not cover terminal sterilisation of drug products, only aseptic processing and the sterilisation of components, containers, closures and equipment. It holds that aseptic processing should be used only where terminal sterilisation is not feasible, although a packaging advantage (for example some dual-chamber syringes) may justify aseptic processing with adjunct steps that raise sterility assurance.
system_implications: Product master data records the sterilisation strategy (terminal, aseptic, or aseptic with an adjunct step) and a reference to the justification when aseptic is chosen. For the terminal-sterilisation configuration of the Injectables edition, requirements must be drawn from other sources (21 CFR 211.113(b), EU Annex 1), because this guidance provides no product-sterilisation rules. Its steriliser principles (IX.C) may be reused by analogy.
verification_test: Create an aseptically filled product with no strategy justification reference: product master approval must be refused. Check that terminal-sterilisation rules in the configuration trace to a source other than this guidance.

requirement: For terminal sterilisation, product is filled and sealed in a high-quality environment so bioburden stays low and the later sterilisation in the final container succeeds. The glossary defines the target sterility assurance level as usually 10^-6, but its parenthetical phrases the probability of a non-sterile unit as greater than one in a million, an apparent inversion: the intended meaning is at most one in a million. An overkill process is defined as giving at least a 12-log reduction of organisms with a D-value of at least 1 minute.
system_implications: The following are inferences for the terminal configuration. The eBMR should capture pre-sterilisation bioburden and enforce a fill-to-sterilisation time limit. It should link every unit (by load, tray or pallet) to a validated load pattern and a cycle record, and store the target SAL (not more than 1 in 10^6) in cycle master data. Configuration text must not copy the glossary's inverted wording.
verification_test: For a terminally sterilised product, exceed the configured fill-to-autoclave time: a deviation must be required. Check that the cycle master data shows SAL as 1E-6 maximum probability of a non-sterile unit.

requirement: Only people authorised by supervisors may enter limited-access areas. A person whom a medical check or a supervisor identifies as ill, or as having open sores, in a way that could affect product quality must not have direct contact with components, containers, closures, in-process materials and product until the condition is resolved or cleared by competent medical staff. Staff must report such health conditions to their supervisor.
system_implications: Aseptic-area sign-in checks that the person is on the supervisor-authorised access list and records a health self-declaration. Supervisors or medical staff can set an exclusion flag that blocks the person from product-contact steps until a clearance is recorded. The flag state at the time of each signature is kept in the batch record.
verification_test: Set a medical exclusion on an operator: filling-step signatures must be refused until a clearance with a medical reference is recorded. A user not on the access list must be refused aseptic sign-in.

requirement: Instruments, apparatus, gauges and recorders must be calibrated at suitable intervals under a written program with directions, schedules, accuracy and precision limits, and remedial actions. Any that do not meet specifications must not be used.
system_implications: Every instrument whose reading enters the batch record is referenced by ID and checked against the calibration system at the moment of use. This includes balances, fill-weight checkweighers, particle counters, air samplers, integrity testers, steriliser and tunnel sensors, dP gauges and incubators. Readings from overdue or failed instruments are refused, or accepted only as a deviation with a retrospective impact assessment once the instrument's as-found calibration is known.
verification_test: Record a fill-weight check on a balance whose calibration expired yesterday: the entry must be refused or deviation-gated. Record an as-found out-of-tolerance result on an integrity tester: all results since its last good calibration must be listed for impact assessment.

requirement: When needed, samples must be collected with sterile equipment and aseptic technique.
system_implications: Sampling steps on sterile materials, such as sterile bulk, sterile API, and in-process samples taken after sterile filtration, record the sterile sampling device or container used and its sterilisation record, the aseptic sampling method or SOP, the location or class, and the sampler's qualification. Steps without these cannot be completed.
verification_test: Record a post-filtration bulk sample without the sampling-device sterilisation reference: completion must be refused.

section: X and XI (text boxes); IV.E; IX.A.1
requirement: To ensure batch uniformity and integrity, written procedures must be established and followed for the in-process controls, tests or examinations performed on samples of in-process material from each batch. These controls must monitor output and validate the performance of process steps that can cause variability. In aseptic filling this includes fill weight or volume checks, which the guidance prefers automated (in-line) to reduce interventions.
system_implications: The MBR defines each IPC with frequency, sample size, method, equipment and limits, for example fill weight or volume, stopper and seal checks, and container-closure checks. The eBMR schedules IPCs by time or unit count, captures results (preferably automatically from in-line checkweighers), enforces limits and reaction rules, and flags missed IPCs. Manual weight checks inside the critical zone are logged as interventions.
verification_test: Miss a scheduled 15-minute fill-weight check: the missed IPC must be flagged. Record a manual weight check in the ISO 5 zone: it must also be recorded as an intervention with duration.

requirement: Records must be kept so their data can be used, at least once a year, to evaluate each product's quality standards and decide whether specifications or manufacturing or control procedures need to change.
system_implications: Injectables data are held as structured, queryable data so the annual product review can be produced without re-keying: interventions (type, count, duration), EM and personnel-monitoring excursions, time-limit exceedances, filter integrity failures, sterilisation deviations, media-fill results, sterility and endotoxin results, and investigations per product and line.
verification_test: Generate a 12-month APR extract for one product and check that intervention counts, EM excursions and sterility results match the source batch records.

requirement: Aseptic processing areas must have, as appropriate: smooth, hard, cleanable floors, walls and ceilings; temperature and humidity control; HEPA-filtered air supplied under positive pressure; a system for monitoring environmental conditions; a cleaning and disinfection system for rooms and equipment; and a system for maintaining the equipment that controls aseptic conditions. Equipment to control air pressure, micro-organisms, dust, humidity and temperature must be provided where appropriate.
system_implications: This is the regulatory basis for linking environmental data to the batch. Beyond dP, particles and viables, the eBMR links room temperature and relative humidity for the batch window, compares them with room limits, and flags excursions. It also links the room's cleaning and disinfection status and the maintenance status of HVAC and critical-zone units.
verification_test: Inject an RH excursion above the room limit during compounding: it must appear in the batch environment section needing assessment. Mark the HVAC unit preventive maintenance as overdue: line clearance must flag it.

requirement: How long a media fill runs should depend on the time needed to include the manipulations and interventions, and on how long the real aseptic operation lasts. Common interventions should be simulated in routine media fills, and rare ones can be simulated periodically.
system_implications: Each intervention catalogue entry has a frequency class (common or rare), the date it was last simulated, and the required simulation interval. When an intervention is performed in production, the eBMR checks that its type was simulated within its interval: every routine media fill for common types, and a defined period for rare types. Otherwise it flags a deviation.
verification_test: Mark 'filling pump replacement' as rare with a 24-month interval and last simulated 30 months ago, then log it in production: a deviation must be raised. Log a common intervention simulated in the last media fill: no flag.

requirement: Concern about nutrient medium contaminating the facility is addressed by handling the medium properly and promptly following each media fill with cleaning, sanitising and, where needed, sterilisation of the equipment. Done this way, later product runs are unlikely to be compromised.
system_implications: When a media-fill batch closes, the line and its equipment are set to 'post-media-fill clean required'. The eBMR blocks the next commercial batch on that line until the cleaning, sanitisation and sterilisation records for the affected equipment and room are complete. The time between media-fill end and cleaning is recorded against a configured maximum.
verification_test: Close a media fill and immediately schedule a commercial fill on the same line: the start must be blocked until the post-media-fill clean records are signed.

name: Area and zone classification register
purpose: Master data for every room, critical zone, isolator interior and background area: its class, limits and qualification state. Used to check that each step runs in a room of the right class, and to link environmental data to the batch.
fields: zone_type (critical ISO 5 / isolator interior / background / support / unclassified)
rules: Limits default to Table 1 values and can only be changed through change control with a justification
Alert level must always be below action level (glossary definition), otherwise the configuration is rejected
Each MBR step declares a minimum class, and execution in a lower-class zone is blocked
An expired qualification, HEPA certification or velocity check blocks or deviation-gates line clearance
The status in effect at execution time is stored in the batch record

name: Batch environmental window
purpose: Automatically attaches to the batch all environmental and facility data (particles, viable EM, dP, temperature/RH, alarms, power events) for every room and zone the batch used, over the time it was in use.
rules: The window runs from the first to the last aseptic activity in each room, plus a configurable margin
A gap in a data feed is treated as an alarm and needs assessment
Any ISO 5 viable recovery or power event automatically opens a deviation linked to the batch
Every excursion or alarm needs a documented assessment before the section can be signed
QA release is blocked until the section is signed

name: Aseptic personnel roster and qualification gate
purpose: Records every person who entered the aseptic area during the batch (operators, set-up, maintenance, samplers). Checks each person's qualifications at entry and at every signature.
rules: Sign-in and e-signature are refused if gowning qualification is expired or suspended, training is missing, the last media fill is more than 12 months old or did not cover the activity, the person is not authorised, or an exclusion flag is set
The qualification snapshot is stored with every signature
If headcount exceeds the maximum qualified in the media fill, a deviation is raised
The roster is printed or rendered in the executed batch record

name: Personnel monitoring sampler
purpose: Generates and tracks glove and gown surface samples for each aseptic operator, and links their results and follow-up to every batch the operator worked on.
fields: sites (left/right glove fingers, forearm, chest, mask, etc.)
trigger (critical-zone exit / end of session / post-intervention / isolator glove port)
rules: Glove samples are taken at least daily or per lot for every roster member, and gown sites at the configured frequency
High-intervention operators get extra sampling tasks
A glove sanitisation within the configured interval before sampling triggers a warning and needs a justification or re-sample
Batch review is blocked until all personnel monitoring results have come back and been assessed
An action-level result opens an investigation linked to every batch that person worked in the session and sets their requalification status

name: Intervention catalogue
purpose: Master data per line listing every permitted aseptic intervention, with the rules for performing it, documenting it and qualifying it through media fills.
rules: Interventions not in the catalogue can only be recorded through a deviation
Units removed in a media fill may never exceed the number defined for production
Common types must have been simulated in the latest routine media fill, and rare types within their interval
Catalogue changes need QA approval and change control

name: Intervention and stoppage log
purpose: Records every line stoppage and aseptic intervention during execution, with time, duration and detail proportionate to risk. Used to review the batch and to compare it with the media-fill envelope.
rules: PLC or SCADA machine stops are reconciled with log entries, and unmatched stops are flagged for review
Exceeding the catalogue maximum duration, or a clearance-required type, forces a line clearance record before restart
Corrective or major interventions require the extended fields
Each operator's media-fill coverage for the intervention type is checked
Events appear on a timeline with particle and viable data in the review dossier

name: Time-limit rule engine
purpose: Defines, runs and enforces the data-supported time limits for each phase of sterile manufacture (211.111). Timers start and stop automatically from recorded events.
rules: Standard templates: compounding start to filtration start; total filtration time; filtered-bulk hold to fill end; product exposure on the line; sterile equipment, container and closure holds; stopper wash to sterilisation; stopper to crimp; fill to lyophiliser loading; dirty-hold and clean-hold; prefilter use time; fill to terminal sterilisation (terminal configuration)
The MBR cannot be approved while any rule lacks a validation reference
An exceedance blocks downstream steps until a deviation with a justification is approved by QA
A time-limit compliance summary is included in the review dossier

name: Sterilisation and depyrogenation cycle record
purpose: Links each steriliser, oven, tunnel, SIP, EtO or irradiation cycle, with its load, parameters and evidence, to the items and batches it served. Makes sure every load followed a validated load pattern.
fields: actuals (temperature, pressure, time at temperature, F0 or lethality, belt speed, come-up time)
rules: The equipment must be qualified and not overdue for requalification or preventive maintenance, and must have no open change control
The load must match the selected validated pattern, and the recipe must be linked to that pattern
Any parameter outside its validated range fails the load and blocks use of its items
Instruments feeding the record must be in calibration
Come-up time is compared with the validated range and trended
Manual valve steps are completed as an ordered, attributed checklist

name: Sterile item status and genealogy
purpose: Tracks the status and hold-time expiry of every sterilised or depyrogenated item (equipment parts, tools, containers, closures, ready-to-use components) and its path into the batch.
fields: status (dirty / clean / dried / sterile / in use / expired)
rules: Items without a valid sterile status cannot be used in any ISO 5 step
Items past their hold expiry are blocked unless a deviation is approved
Equipment is re-sterilised for every batch unless a validated campaign rule exists
Container and closure lots need a complete preparation record before they are issued to the filler
Ready-to-use items need a CoA, a sterilisation certificate and a current supplier reliability status

name: Filter register and integrity test record
purpose: Tracks each sterilising, clarifying, vent, gas and HEPA filter: its validation fit, usage, integrity tests and link to batches, so a filter failure can be traced to every affected batch.
fields: filter_role (product sterilising / redundant / prefilter / vent / gas / HEPA)
validated_envelope (max dP, flow, temperature, contact time, volume, lots)
post_use_test (type, tester_id, wetting_fluid, temperature, test_pressure, value, product-specific limit, result, printout)
rules: A part number not validated for the product cannot be installed
A filter used once cannot be reused unless validated for reuse, and never beyond the validated number of lots
A passing post-use integrity test is required before filtered bulk is released to filling or the batch goes to review
The integrity-test limit comes from master data and cannot be typed in
A failed test opens a deviation, puts the batch on hold, and links every batch since the filter's last passing test
Vent and gas filters are blocked past their replacement interval

name: Process simulation (media fill) record
purpose: An executed record for each media-fill run, kept separate from commercial batches, that documents conditions, simulated activities, accounting of every unit, incubation and interpretation.
fields: positives (tray / time block, organism to species)
rules: Incubation must stay within 20-35 C and within 2.5 C of target, for at least 14 days in total and at least 7 days per phase with the lower temperature first
The record cannot close as passed until growth promotion has passed and QC has signed as observer
Outcome follows the run-size criteria, and every positive opens an investigation
Invalidation requires an equivalent rule that applies to commercial lots
On closure the line is set to 'post-media-fill clean required'
The record can never be released as product

name: Line aseptic qualification status and envelope
purpose: Holds each line's (and formulation stage's) process-simulation status and qualified operating envelope. Gates batch starts and compares executed batches against the envelope.
fields: envelope (max aseptic duration, max headcount, allowed intervention types and frequencies, line speed range, formats, shift patterns)
pending_triggers (change controls, shutdowns, EM anomalies, sterility positives)
rules: A fill is blocked if the status is not qualified or requalification is overdue
Executed batches outside the envelope raise a deviation at review
A media-fill failure builds the list of impacted batches since the last pass, holds unreleased ones and flags released ones
Returning to qualified status requires the confirmatory runs chosen by the investigation (three consecutive runs if the root cause is inconclusive)

name: EM sampling plan and task generator
purpose: Turns the written EM program into batch-specific sampling tasks per shift, zone and phase, captures execution evidence, and links results and their evaluation to the batch.
fields: method (active air / settle plate / contact plate / swab / particle)
timing (during / end of operation / after decontamination aeration)
rules: Tasks are generated for every shift the batch spans
Critical-surface samples are released only after fill end, and isolator samples only after aeration end
Settle-plate exposure may not exceed the validated maximum
A missed or late sample is a deviation
Each result is evaluated individually (no averaging); an action-level result needs an evaluation, and critical-zone growth needs an investigation
Organism identification is required for ISO 5, adjacent zones and personnel monitoring
Trend rules (frequency over a window, consecutive hits, new flora) link alerts to batches in the window

name: Sterility and endotoxin release evidence
purpose: Makes sure sterility samples represent the whole fill and processing events, and that sterility and endotoxin results are valid, traceable and correctly dispositioned before release.
rules: Release needs every required pull point, plus approved sterility and endotoxin results within specification that are linked to this batch
A positive sets the batch to presumed non-sterile and puts it on hold
A retest is allowed only after an approved invalidation with conclusive evidence of laboratory cause
An inconclusive investigation allows only rejection
Original results are never overwritten
Results must appear in the executed batch record, not only in the LIMS

name: Contamination investigation evidence pack
purpose: A pre-filled, structured investigation for sterility positives, media-fill positives, critical-zone recoveries and personnel-monitoring action levels. Brings together the evidence the guidance expects and proposes the associated batches required by 211.192.
rules: Evidence sections are populated automatically from batch and system data
The investigation cannot close without an assessment of other batches and products
'Lab error' requires attached conclusive evidence, whatever the lab's track record
EM review must include trends beyond the lot's own day or shift
Isolates are compared using the same identification method

name: Sterile batch review dossier
purpose: The Section XII review package: a holistic assessment of how the process and its supporting systems performed for this production run, with signed-off sections, which gates the QA release e-signature.
fields: utility_data (WFI, clean steam, compressed gases, HVAC/HEPA)
rules: The release e-signature is enabled only when every section is signed and no item is open
Exceptions are highlighted (review by exception), but every underlying record stays one click away
Data gaps count as open items
The contents are frozen at release, and later changes to linked sources create a re-review flag
All in-process and laboratory results must be part of the batch record (211.188)

name: Isolator status and glove integrity register
purpose: Isolator-specific state: decontamination validity, pressure integrity, glove/sleeve/half-suit condition and material transfers, with batch impact logic for breaches.
fields: transfer_log (port type, item, decontamination or sterilisation ref)
rules: Aseptic steps are blocked after 'decontamination valid until'
A breach sets 'decontamination required' and opens a deviation, and units filled in the suspect window default to rejection unless QA justifies otherwise
A failed glove test links every batch since that glove last passed
A signed visual check of each port is required before use
The background room must be classified (typically ISO 8)

name: BFS line control record
purpose: Controls specific to blow-fill-seal that sit alongside the general aseptic rules.
fields: ipc (container weight variation, fill weight, leakers, process air pressure)
rules: SIP and extrusion parameters must be within their validated ranges
Overdue machine preventive maintenance or utility integrity checks block the start
Sampling must cover the entire fill
Significant forming or sealing defects open a 211.192 investigation
Final 100% inspection must be able to detect leakers, with its verification recorded

name: Container-closure inspection and unit reconciliation
purpose: Accounts for every unit from filling to good output, including all removals, and records the 100% inspection results that protect container-closure integrity.
rules: A reconciliation outside tolerance needs a deviation
Release requires 100% inspection to be complete
A critical-defect AQL failure blocks the lot and opens a 211.192 investigation
A trend of container-closure integrity defects prompts procedure improvement
Media-fill reconciliation uses the same structure, with the incubation-specific classes

name: Utility and support-system event register
purpose: Links the state of utilities and support systems (WFI, PW, clean steam, process gases, HVAC, power) and shutdown or return-to-service records to the batches they served.
fields: event_type (alarm / OOS / shutdown / power disruption / maintenance / construction)
rules: Aseptic steps may not start while a shutdown event for the room is open without a return-to-service record
Any power disruption that could affect quality automatically creates a batch deviation (211.100, 211.192)
WFI, clean-steam and gas results in the batch window are listed in the review dossier
Events flagged as media-fill triggers set the line's status to requalification pending
